    <h1>Symmetries of the Dirac equation</h1>
    <p class="course-toc-meta">Topic: Symmetries and Noether&#x27;s theorem</p>
  </header>

::: {.qft-exam-body}
1.  Using Noether's theorem, obtain the conserved current for $$\mathcal{L} =i\bar{\psi}\cancel{\partial}\psi - m\bar{\psi}\psi$$ under the global gauge transformations $$\psi \rightarrow e^{i \alpha} \psi, \,\, \overline{\psi} \rightarrow e^{-i\alpha}  \overline{\psi}.$$

2.  Using Noether's theorem, obtain the conserved current for $\mathcal{L} = i\bar{\psi}\cancel{\partial}\psi$ under the chiral transformation $$\psi \rightarrow e^{i \alpha \gamma^5} \psi.$$ Find how the field $\bar{\psi}$ transforms.

3.  Prove that the action of the massless Dirac field is invariant under dilatations: $$x\to x'=e^{-\rho}x, \quad \psi(x)\to \psi'(x') = e^{3\rho/2}\psi(x).$$ Find the corresponding Noether current and charge.

:::
